newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY GAINS GROUND VS BASKET, ONE-DAY DEPOS DOWN.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY GAINS GROUND VS BASKET, ONE-DAY DEPOS DOWN.

text.p: The Polish zloty strenghtened in thin trade against the basket of currencies after a day of light currency-selling on speculation and small foreign entry into Polish T-bills, dealers said.

They said the zloty did not respond to the dollar's gains against the mark in early trade and tested higher ground despite Thursday's central bank statement that it was happy with the zloty at three percent from the parity rate.
"The zloty made some headway ignoring dollar gains against the mark," said Violetta Gorecka from Pekao SA.

The zloty closed at 3.34/3.30 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Friday's close at 3.15/3.13 percent. It closed at 3.0350/60 to the dollar, down from 3.0310/15 on Friday and at 1.7912/20 to the mark, up from 1.7970/90.
Some players speculatively cut currency exposure as they expected the market might want to test the NBP's words on the preferred zloty level and push it up to 3.5 percent on Tuesday.
"We may see the zloty at 3.5 percent as soon as on Tuesday if nothing special happens to the dollar/mark rate," said Piotr Czyzewski from ING Bank in Warsaw.

Polish CPI rose 2.9 percent in January against a 1.3 percent rise in December, bringing year-on-year inflation down to 18.1 percent. Bankers earlier predicted month-on-month inflation would be 2.3 percent on average.

Dealers said foreign bids at today's primary one-billion zloty T-bill auction were very small. All minimum prices fell aty the tender as the treasury finally sold only 333 million zlotys worth of the bills an a 334 million zloty demand.
The minimum price fall was the deepest on the benchmark 52-week which dropped 0.26 point to 82.90, driving the maximum yield up to 20.40 percent from the previous 20.03 percent.
One-day deposit rates fell in line with better liquidity on the money market from maturing bonds, dealers said.
Overnight rates were quoted at 21.36/21.63 percent, down from opening's 21.90/22.30 percent, tomorrow/next deposits were at 21.46/21.62 percent, down from 21.90/22.40 percent.
